title: Non-right triangles & trigonometry: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Non-right triangles & trigonometry: Visual Guide

1. Drop The Altitude | an oblique triangle cut into two right triangles by the altitude from C, with both readings of that one segment computed live as the two angles are dragged, including the obtuse settings where the foot lands outside the base | the Law of sines is right-triangle trigonometry applied twice to the same altitude, so a side always pairs with the sine of the angle OPPOSITE it, and sin(180 - x) = sin x is why the obtuse case never needed a separate rule

2. Sides Over Sines | the three ratios a/sin A, b/sin B, c/sin C computed independently and shown agreeing to every digit as the angles and the one given side move, switchable between AAS (given side opposite a known angle) and ASA (given side between them), with presets for A=45/B=45/a=8 and A=30/B=60/a=5 | two angles plus any one side is always solvable because the 180 degree sum fixes the shape and the single length fixes the scale, and the shared constant is 2R, the circumdiameter - equal angles therefore force equal opposite sides with no calculation at all

3. The Ambiguous Case | a compass arc of radius a swung from C against the base line, live-counting zero, one or two intersections as the angle A and the opposite side a are dragged, with each surviving triangle drawn and solved | SSA is the configuration that can fit two different triangles, because sin B = sin(180 - B) leaves two candidates whenever the arc reaches the line, and only the comparison of a against the altitude h = b sin A and against b decides how many of them close

4. The Cosine Correction | the term -2ab cos C shown as a signed adjustment to the Pythagorean sum a^2 + b^2 as the included angle sweeps from 1 to 179 degrees, plus an SSS mode that inverts the law for an angle and refuses impossible side triples | the Law of cosines IS the Pythagorean theorem plus one term that vanishes at exactly 90 degrees, it is the law for SAS and SSS, and inverted for an angle it is unambiguous because cosine is one-to-one across the whole 0-180 degree range

5. Which Law First | one live triangle re-framed as each of the six configurations SAS, SSS, ASA, AAS, SSA and AAA, with the given measurements highlighted and the ordered solve plan rewritten with the current numbers | the classification decides the law: a side paired with its opposite angle means the Law of sines can start, no such pair means the Law of cosines must, AAA can never be solved because nothing fixes the size, and solving a general triangle or a word problem always means producing all six measurements
